HatchPattern__Concrete__Meta.Meta__Description: Concrete in section - small open triangles for the aggregate, scattered through a stipple of dots for the fines. Slabs, foundations, padstones, lintels.
HatchPattern__Concrete__Meta.Meta__WhyPaperUnits: Every length here is PAPER millimetres, like the dash patterns in Na__LayoutEditor__EdgeStyles__Config__.json, so the hatch measures the same on the sheet at 1:20 and at 1:100. Pattern scale adjusts from there.
HatchPattern__Concrete__Meta.Meta__WhyScatter: The positions are a blue-noise scatter, generated ONCE and written in below as fixed numbers, so screen and paper can never disagree. It was scored on a torus - the gap across a tile seam counts like any other gap - and against the regularities that survive a repeat: two marks sharing a column (an endless vertical line once the tile repeats) or a row. A lattice was never an option: it lays visible stripes across a wall.
HatchPattern__Concrete__Meta.Meta__WhyInsideTheTile: Every mark sits wholly inside the tile, so nothing crosses a seam at all: a browser clips a <pattern> at its tile edge and the PDF stamper does not.
HatchPattern__Concrete__Meta.Meta__WhyThreeTriangles: Three triangles, each a different shape at a different turn, so no two neighbours match and the field does not read as a wallpaper of one stamp.

HatchPattern__Concrete__Identity.Identity__Description: How this pattern is named, found and grouped in the pattern lists.
HatchPattern__Concrete__Identity.Identity__Note: The standard section hatch for in-situ concrete: aggregate triangles in a stipple of fines.

HatchPattern__Concrete__Tile.Tile__Description: The repeating cell, in paper millimetres.
HatchPattern__Concrete__Tile.Tile__Note: Seven triangles and eighteen dots: about one mark to every 16 square millimetres.

HatchPattern__Concrete__Defaults.Defaults__Description: What the pattern draws with until a use sets its own. The stroke is 0.35 pt (0.1235 mm) at scale 1 and grows with the pattern scale; a line weight typed in the panel does not. 'inherit' takes the colour of whatever carries the hatch - a vector's edge colour - until a pattern colour is picked.

HatchPattern__Concrete__Glyphs.Glyphs__Description: Drawn about the glyph's own origin, y pointing DOWN, in tile millimetres. Strokes only: the PDF stamps a tile as lines and never fills one.

TriangleB.Glyph__Note: Turned about a third of a turn from the first.

TriangleC.Glyph__Note: Smaller, so the aggregate reads as graded.

Dot.Glyph__Note: A tenth of a millimetre of line: with round caps it prints as a dot the width of the line weight. A true zero-length line is left out by some PDF viewers.

HatchPattern__Concrete__Bounds.Bounds__Description: How far a use may scale and turn this pattern before it stops reading as the material.
